stem:
Malini looks at the graph of morning and afternoon temperatures over four days.

Which claim correctly states what the axes, scale, and legend represent before any values are compared?

options.text: The solid line is morning temperature and the dashed line is afternoon temperature; the vertical axis shows temperature in $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ with equal scale marks.
The plotted points can be read with no use of the axis scales or the legend.
The temperature scale is what the legend creates from the morning and afternoon labels.
The solid line shows afternoon temperature and the dashed line shows morning temperature.

teacher.key_rationale: Read legend and axes first: solid=morning, dashed=afternoon, vertical scale in °C. Skipping scales/legend, reversing legend as cause of the scale, or swapping legend labels all miss the read-structure hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source pie chart as a two-series line graph with day axis, °C scale, markers, and morning/afternoon legend.
